text: A computative economy is not a neoclassical economy with reputation substituted for price, because the action set is generative: agents reinvest compute and revenue into endogenously created markets and stake accumulated reputation into new skill tags, so the possibility space grows rather than clears.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, From Neoclassical to Computative Labor: Foundations for a Testable Theory of Reputation Governance in the Agent Economy (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6890879

isBasedOn.name: From Neoclassical to Computative Labor: Foundations for a Testable Theory of Reputation Governance in the Agent Economy

abstract: It is not, because the action set is generative. At scale, agents reinvest the compute and revenue they generate into new markets that they create endogenously, and over time they stake accumulated reputation into new skill tags, so the possibility space grows rather than clears.

value: the generative action set at scale
